overview: Caral in Peru's Supe Valley preserves a major early center of organized settlement. Monumental architecture and its urban layout provide evidence of collective labor and ceremonial activity.

items.text: Radiocarbon work places the development of the site approximately between 3000 and 1800 BCE. This is a settlement sequence, not a pair of precisely known royal dates.
Builders created substantial platform mounds from earth and stone. Their construction formed a durable framework for the city's ceremonial spaces.
Sunken circular courts were integrated with elevated platforms. Repeated forms helped organize the relationship between built masses and gathering places.
The city's plan and monumental structures indicate ceremonial functions. UNESCO interprets them as evidence of a strongly organized religious and political center.
Later occupation was limited and largely peripheral. The preservation of the earlier core lets archaeologists study a long sequence of urban development.
